title: The Driver Who 'Cuts In' Is Doing It Right (Zipper Merge)
description:
The driver who stays in the closing lane to the end and then merges? In heavy, slow traffic, that's exactly what road agencies ask for. Using both lanes and taking turns at the merge point can make the backup up to 40% shorter.

Honest catch: Minnesota's transport department says it won't get you through the road works faster. It makes the queue shorter, evens out both lanes and cuts risky lane-jumping. In light traffic, merge early.

Sources:
- Minnesota Department of Transportation, 'LATE MERGE ... the ZIPPER SYSTEM' (work zone guidance, 2008), dot.state.mn.us/trafficeng/workzone/doc/When-latemerge-zipper.pdf
- Wisconsin Department of Transportation, 'Zipper merge', wisconsindot.gov/Pages/safety/safety-eng/ZipperMerge.aspx (accessed 2026-11-20)

How it's made: original 3D characters and scenes, animated by us. The voices are AI voices (ElevenLabs).

Counterphysical: traffic science that breaks your intuition.
